City Hall unveils streetcar extension to Ponce City Market

The city on Tuesday released its plan to extend the downtown streetcar east along Edgewood Avenue and up the Eastside Trail to Ponce City Market. Planners say the line could carry 10,000 riders a day once it opens, and that trains would run every 10 minutes during the morning rush.

The extension would be built for about $190 million, most of it from a federal grant. Officials estimate the cost works out to roughly $5.50 per rider over twenty years.

Supporters argue the line would save commuters in the Old Fourth Ward about 12 minutes each way and take cars off Ponce de Leon Avenue. Critics are not convinced; one neighborhood association called the schedule optimistic.

The council is expected to vote on the plan next month.
